title: Marching Huey Long from Union Station and the parade pay
summary: The band led Huey from the station to the hotel, playing the same number, for parade pay of a few dollars for a full day.

story.theme_name: Brass bands, parades and jazz funerals
story.community_name: Parading for Mardi Gras and the clubs

blocks.x: Man, we were deep out of the train. Everybody got off the train. And they had his, like white guard fellas. Big shot fellas. That's all. He came marching now. He marched with him. He marched all the way from the station to the Roseville. Swing along with him. He was Grand Norse. Oh, Hugh, he would be out in front? Yeah, he was Grand Norse. Oh, I see. He'd lead the band. Yeah, man. People used to clock and everything. Man, man, man. We'd play that number man always from there to the Roseville. That would be the station. What station did you come in? Union Station. Union Station. Illinois Central or something. Gee, that's quite a ways to work. Oh, that's a fire.
Well, that's not so fire. I mean, for Hughie, it'd be eight to ten blocks.

It's summer hot, summertime, man. That little hotel, little dope fella there. Probably in Sydney. Come round by the headquarters. Bam! Bam! Bam! Man, you used to come in, like, a lot of boys be there. You know, stomach build regular. That stuff. Yeah. I kept wearing that new coat, man. Come on. Kick my horn, you know. I won't get back there in time, man. Yeah. Now, you see, I used to get a kick out of that. Yeah. That's good. That wasn't good enough. So, man. Always seventeen dollars. Yeah. Parade all day long around the street then, man, for five dollars. Go to tenement parade and all that business. All day long. Yeah.
Tenenteen dollars then would be worth a lot of money.
Man, the kick would get out of it, you know. Freshman and all that, you know. I actually like to hear him talk and all that, too. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm. Mm-hm.
